In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Muzzammil

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who wrap yourself [in garments]!﴾ ﴿Stand [in prayer] at night, except a little.﴾

He, may He be exalted, explained the amount whose standing is required by what follows: ﴿half of it, or reduce from it [a little]﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 3], i.e., from half of it, or add to it, i.e., to half of it. In this noble verse and what follows it there is an explanation of the general statement of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And from the night, pray with it as an additional [devotion] for you﴾ [al-Isra': 79], and so on.

In it there is also an explanation of the manner of standing [in prayer], which is by reciting the Qur'an measuredly (tartil), and in it there is a response to two issues on which opinions differ.

The first of them: the number of rak'ahs of the night prayer (qiyam al-layl). Is it eight rak'ahs or more?

The Prophet ﷺ was given the choice between these times of the night, and he left that to his energy, readiness and comfort. Therefore it is not possible to worship by a specific number that is not valid apart from it, nor is it permissible to exceed it. There has been disagreement concerning the night prayer of Ramadan in particular, and the better course is to adopt what the earlier generations (al-salaf) approved. We have already presented on this question a general treatise, the Risalat al-Tarawih, more than a thousand years ago in the Mosque of the Prophet ﷺ, and the practice has settled at twenty [rak'ahs] in Ramadan.

The second issue: what the jurists mention regarding the manner of the night prayer in general: is it better to have many rak'ahs, because of the abundance of bowing and prostration, since the closest a servant comes to Allah is while he is prostrating; or a long standing for recitation, since the reciter receives ten good deeds for every letter? Here His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And recite the Qur'an in measured recitation﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 4] states explicitly that what counts is reciting the Qur'an measuredly (tartil), and He emphasized it with the verbal noun (tartilan) to affirm this meaning, as Ibn Mas'ud said: "Do not scatter it like the scattering of sand, nor rush through it like the rushing of poetry. Stop at its wonders, and move hearts with it, and let not the greatest concern of any one of you be the end of the surah."

And Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her, described the recitation of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by saying: "He would divide his recitation verse by verse: ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾ ﴿Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ ﴿The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾ ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾ [al-Fatihah: 4]." Narrated by Ahmad.

(p-٣٥٨) And in the Sahih, from Anas: he was asked about the recitation of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "It was elongated (madd). Then he recited: ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾, lengthening [the sound of] 'Bismillah', lengthening 'al-Rahman', and lengthening 'al-Rahim'."

Note.

Tajwid has known limits for elongation (madd) according to what the reciters have received, may Allah have mercy on them. Whatever exceeds them is trifling, and whatever falls short of them is a failure in the due right of recitation.

From this it is known that those who treat the Qur'an like anything else in manner of delivery, with drawling and excess, have not observed the meaning of this noble verse. This does not preclude beautifying the voice in recitation, as in his ﷺ saying: "Adorn the Qur'an with your voices."

And Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him, said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "If I had known that you were listening to my recitation, I would have embellished it for you with embellishment." This quality is what achieves the purpose of recitation, which is reflection and contemplation, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do they not reflect upon the Qur'an?﴾ [al-Nisa': 82]. It is also the quality with which the purpose of humbling the heart is achieved, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement, a Book consistent and oft-repeated, at which shiver the skins of those who fear their Lord; then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah﴾ [al-Zumar: 23]. Hearts and skins are not affected by it unless it is recited measuredly. If it were recited like poetry or ordinary speech, it would not be understood; and if it were recited melodiously like songs, it would not have effect. Therefore measured recitation is obligatory, as the Prophet ﷺ explained.

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

(p-٤٢٦) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Muzzammil

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who wrap yourself [in garments]!﴾ ﴿Stand [in prayer] at night, except a little.﴾

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] almost two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it, and [so do] a group of those with you﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 20]. It indicates the obligation of the night prayer upon the community, because a command to the exemplar is a command to his followers.

And His saying: ﴿and a group of those with you﴾ is evidence that it is not specific to him ﷺ.

Allah has mentioned what indicates the opposite of that in His saying: ﴿So recite what is easy of the Qur'an﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 20], and His saying: ﴿So recite what is easy from it﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 20]. The answer is clear: the latter abrogates the former, and then the latter was also abrogated by the five daily prayers.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We are going to cast upon you a weighty word﴾.

It is well known that the "word" here is the Qur'an, as Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, it is the speech of a noble messenger﴾ [al-Haqqah: 40], and His saying: ﴿And We have certainly conveyed to them the word, that perhaps they may be reminded﴾ [al-Qasas: 51].

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, it is a decisive word﴾ [al-Tariq: 13], and His saying: ﴿And who is more truthful than Allah in statement?﴾ [al-Nisa': 122], and similar verses.

However, describing it as "weighty" is notable, since weight pertains to measurable things (al-awzan, "weights"), which are perceptible objects.

Some exegetes (mufassirun, plural of mufassir, one who performs tafsir, i.e., Qur'anic exegesis) said: the weight lies in the reward of it. It was also said that it lies in its obligations (al-takalif), and it was said that it lies in what accompanies its descent upon him. All of this is established for the noble Qur'an. As for its descent, it is established that when the revelation came to him (ﷺ), he would be overtaken by severe distress, and his face would turn red as if it were a gilded thing (mudhhabah). When it descended upon him (ﷺ) while he was on a journey on his mount, the she-camel would kneel down with him. And it is related from Anas: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was resting his head on his thigh, when the revelation came to him. Anas said: My thigh was nearly separated from me."

As for its obligations, they were heavy upon the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, and they feared it, as is well known.

As for its reward, it has come in the hadith of Muslim: "Al-hamdu lillah (praise be to Allah) fills the scale, and Subhan Allah (Glory be to Allah) and al-hamdu lillah together fill, or fill what is between the heavens and the earth."

The hadith of the scroll (al-bitaqah) and all of this, some of it bears witness to the other and does not contradict it.

Allah, Exalted is He, has also made clear that this weight may be lightened by Allah for the believers, as in the prayer, in His saying: ﴿And indeed, it is difficult except for the humble, who are certain that they will meet their Lord﴾ [al-Baqarah: 45–46]. Likewise, the Qur'an is heavy upon the disbelievers, but light upon the believers, who love it.

It has come in reports that some of the early generations (al-salaf) would spend the entire night standing in prayer with a single surah of the Qur'an, out of delight and joy, as Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance﴾ [al-Qamar: 17]. So it is heavy in its weight and heavy in its obligations, but Allah lightens it and makes it easy for whoever He guides and grants success to it.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 73, verse 6:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the rising at night is more effective in tread and more upright in speech.﴾

That is: what one establishes of night prayer (qiyam al-layl) is more conducive to the heart's agreement (with the Qur'an), and more upright in speech in recitation, reflection (tadabbur) and contemplation (ta'ammul), and consequently in being affected (by it). In it there is guidance toward what counters this weight of the word that will be cast upon him, for it serves as direction toward what one provisions oneself with to bear the weight of the burdens of the call (da'wah) and the message (risalah).

I heard from our Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, his saying: The Qur'an does not become firm in the breast, nor is its memorization made easy, nor its understanding made smooth, except by standing in worship with it in the depths of the night. He, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, never abandoned his nightly portion (wird), whether in summer or in winter. This meaning is conveyed by the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 45]. So when a matter distressed the Prophet (ﷺ), he would turn to prayer.

Likewise here, the rising at night was an aid to him (ﷺ) against the weight of the word that would be cast upon him.

Question:

It has been said: standing in the night was obligatory upon the Prophet (ﷺ) before the five daily prayers were prescribed, based on His saying: ﴿And from the night, perform tahajjud with it as a supererogatory (nafilah) for you﴾ [al-Isra': 79]. Nafilah means an addition. It has also been said: it was obligatory upon him (ﷺ) and upon the generality of the Muslims, based on His saying in this surah: ﴿Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand (in prayer) nearly two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it, and a group of those with you﴾. Then He lightened all of this by His saying: ﴿So He has turned to you; so recite what is easy of the Qur'an﴾, up to His saying: ﴿So recite what is easy of it, and establish prayer, give zakah, and loan Allah a goodly loan. And whatever good you put forward for yourselves, you will find it with Allah, better and greater in reward﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 20].

However, when he (ﷺ) undertook an act, he would persist in it. Thus he would stand in the night out of gratitude to Allah, as in the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her: "Shall I not be a grateful servant?" It remained a sunnah for others according to what is within their ability. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 73, verse 14:

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the mountains will be a heap of sand, poured forth﴾.

It does not contradict His saying: ﴿And the mountains will be like wool, fluffed up﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 5], because His saying ﴿And the mountains became a heap of sand, poured forth﴾ is an eloquent simile (tashbih baligh). The mountains, after their being crushed, which is stated in His saying ﴿And the mountains will be pulverized, pulverized﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 5 (15 in the Arabic numbering)], resemble loose, flowing sand, and they also resemble fluffed-up wool.
